Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jamie Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, CTO; Mike Patel, Chief Revenue Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jamie Thompson.

Jamie Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on six key areas: customer mix trends, NRR performance, cash position and runway, capital allocation strategy, free cash flow generation, and operating margin expansion. Sarah will provide the detailed metrics and insights on these shortly.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss the financials in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jamie. As Jamie mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $285 million, representing a 42% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income came in robustly at $52 million on a non-GAAP basis.

Turning first to our customer mix trends, which continue to be a key driver of our predictable, high-quality revenue growth. We've strategically positioned CloudForge as a scalable customer data platform tailored for both high-volume SMB adoption and mission-critical enterprise deployments. Our customer base now spans over 12,500 logos globally, with a deliberate shift toward enterprise customers that deliver outsized economics.

Let me break this down with the latest metrics from Q3. Total ARR ended the quarter at $428 million, up 38% year-over-year. By segment: Enterprise customers, defined as those with ACV over $100K, represent 68% of total ARR, up from 62% a year ago and 55% two years back. We added 47 net new enterprise logos in Q3 alone, including several Fortune 500 names like a major U.S. bank and a European telco giant. Average ACV for these customers hit $450K, reflecting multi-year contracts with advanced features like our AI-powered Real-Time Identity Resolution and Snowflake Marketplace integrations. Dollar-based net retention here remains elite at 128%, driven by expansions into adjacent use cases such as predictive churn modeling and personalized marketing orchestration.

SMB and mid-market, with ACV under $100K, account for 32% of ARR, stable sequentially but up modestly 5% YoY in absolute dollars to $137 million. We onboarded 1,200 net new SMB customers in the quarter, fueled by our self-serve Freemium tier and viral adoption via our Partner Marketplace, which now includes over 300 ISV integrations like Zapier and Segment alternatives. Churn here is low at 4% annually, with NRR at 112%—solid for the segment, thanks to upsell paths into our Pro tier with features like HIPAA-compliant data lakes for healthcare SMBs.

This mix evolution is no accident; it's the result of our land-and-expand playbook, honed over the past 18 months. Enterprise ARR grew 52% YoY, outpacing SMB's 22%, as we've invested heavily in technical initiatives to meet Fortune 1000 demands. For instance, our Q2 launch of FedRAMP Moderate authorization unlocked U.S. public sector deals, contributing 15% of new enterprise bookings. We've also scaled our Kubernetes-native architecture on AWS and Azure to handle petabyte-scale data volumes without performance degradation—critical for enterprises running complex CDP stacks alongside tools like Salesforce Data Cloud or Adobe Real-Time CDP.

Regionally, the trends vary tellingly: North America, 82% of ARR, is enterprise-heavy at 75% mix, with hyperscaler partnerships accelerating wins, think integrations with Databricks for AI workloads, mirroring Snowflake's momentum. EMEA, 12% of ARR, is SMB-led at 55% mix, growing 45% YoY on GDPR-ready features and channel partnerships with resellers like Ingram Micro; enterprise penetration is rising post-Brexit, with key logos in fintech hubs like Frankfurt. APAC, 6% of ARR and fastest-growing at 68% YoY, is balanced at 50/50, but SMB volume is exploding via Tokyo and Singapore data centers; we're targeting verticals like e-commerce with Shopify integrations to mirror HubSpot's mid-market success there, while piloting enterprise POCs with banks in Mumbai.

Strategically, we're doubling down on enterprise for margin expansion—gross margins hit 81% this quarter, with enterprise cohorts at 85% vs. SMB's 76%, due to lower support intensity and higher automation. That said, SMB remains our growth engine for net new logos and a farm system for expansions; over 20% of Q3 enterprise deals were upsells from SMB roots. Looking ahead, we expect enterprise to reach 72% of ARR by year-end FY25, supported by $50 million in R&D for GenAI agents that automate CDP orchestration—think autonomous customer 360 views rivaling ServiceNow's Vancouver release. This balanced mix de-risks our model amid macro headwinds: SMB resilience cushions enterprise sales cycles now averaging 4-6 months, while enterprise stickiness delivers cohort LTVs exceeding 5x CAC. We're well-positioned against peers—our enterprise NRR tops Salesforce's 120% benchmark—setting up for sustained 35%+ ARR growth into 2025.

Next, on NRR performance, I'm pleased to report that in Q3 FY24, our Net Revenue Retention—or NRR—came in at 118%, marking our strongest quarterly performance in over a year and up 600 basis points sequentially from 112% in Q2. On a year-over-year basis, this represents an 800 basis point improvement from 110% in Q3 FY23. For context, this places us at the upper end of our peer set, comparable to high performers like Snowflake at around 120% or Datadog in the mid-110s, while we continue to outperform legacy players like Oracle's cloud cohort, which has hovered in the high 90s.

To break this down, our NRR reflects a healthy mix of expansion offsetting moderate churn and contraction pressures. Starting with the numerator: from our Q2-ending ARR cohort, we delivered net expansion equating to a robust 28% expansion rate. This was driven primarily by two vectors. First, usage-based upsells within our core Workflow Automation platform, where customers scaling AI-powered modules like our ForgeAI Predictor—our generative AI tool for predictive workflow optimization—accounted for 45% of expansion dollars. We've seen this particularly in enterprise accounts mirroring ServiceNow's Vancouver release dynamics, where IT ops teams expand from basic orchestration to full-stack AI orchestration. Second, cross-sell success into adjacent products: 35% of expansion came from net new seats in our Forge Security module, fueled by our Q2 launch of zero-trust integrations with Okta and CrowdStrike, landing us 120 deals averaging $250K ACV upsell.

On the downside, gross dollar churn was 6%, primarily from SMB and mid-market segments amid ongoing macro headwinds. This was flat sequentially but down from 8% YoY, reflecting our sharpened focus on customer health scores. Key churn drivers included a few logo losses in the retail vertical, where inflationary pressures forced consolidation onto cheaper alternatives like monday.com. However, our enterprise churn remained sub-2%, with no losses over $1 million ACV, underscoring the stickiness of our platform in mission-critical environments.

Contraction weighed in at 4%, largely from pricing resets and usage normalization post our FY23 land-and-expand ramp. About 60% stemmed from annual true-ups where customers right-sized seats after hyper-growth phases, akin to what we've seen industry-wide with Zoominfo or HubSpot cohorts. Positively, proactive customer success interventions—via our expanded CS team now at 250 reps with AI-driven churn prediction models—recovered 15% of at-risk contractions, converting 22 accounts from downsell to flat or expansion.

Regionally, this NRR was propelled by U.S. strength at 122%, where hyperscaler partnerships with AWS Bedrock and Azure OpenAI have accelerated AI module adoption among Fortune 1000 firms. EMEA contributed 115%, bolstered by GDPR-compliant ForgeAI rollouts and a 25% YoY increase in expansion from DACH enterprises investing in digital transformation despite ECB rate hikes. APAC lagged at 108%, pressured by yen depreciation and delayed RFPs in Japan, though our Singapore hub's localization efforts—including Mandarin UI and Tencent Cloud integrations—stemmed churn to under 5%.

Strategically, these results validate our AI Everywhere pivot. We've invested $50 million in R&D to embed agentic AI across our stack, driving cohort NRR for FY23 signings to 125% already in their first full quarter—outpacing vintage 2022 cohorts at 110%. Looking forward, we expect Q4 NRR of 119-121%, with expansion scaling to 30% as ForgeAI hits general availability and we launch premium tiers at $0.05 per AI inference, tapping the $20 billion enterprise AI ops market per Gartner. Churn discipline remains key; we're targeting sub-5% via our revamped onboarding playbook, which has lifted Day 90 activation rates to 92%.

In summary, our 118% NRR signals durable growth from existing customers, even in a cautious IT spend environment, positioning CloudForge to deliver on our $1.2 billion FY24 ARR guide with confidence.

Now, regarding our cash position and expected cash runway—in the SaaS landscape, cash is king, especially in a market where enterprise buyers are extending sales cycles amid macroeconomic headwinds like elevated interest rates and selective IT spend. As of September 30th, 2024, we ended the quarter with $452 million in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments. This represents a sequential increase of $28 million from Q2, driven primarily by stronger-than-expected cash collections on our expanding ARR base and disciplined operating leverage.

Operating cash flow came in at $42 million for the quarter, a $15 million improvement quarter-over-quarter. This was underpinned by collections acceleration: DSO improved to 58 days from 64 in Q2, thanks to enhanced AR management via our own platform tools, which we've deployed internally. Dollar-based net retention held steady at 118%, reflecting upsell momentum in our Enterprise tier, where customers are layering on AI modules at a 25% attach rate. Margin expansion also played a role: Non-GAAP operating margins hit 12%, ahead of our guidance, as we realized 18% sequential savings in sales & marketing through a pivot to high-ROI channels like partner ecosystems, for example our deepened AWS Marketplace integration, mirroring Snowflake's co-sell playbook.

On the uses side, capex remained modest at $8 million, or 1.8% of revenue, focused on data center expansions in AWS and Azure to support our multi-tenant architecture scaling to 99.99% uptime SLAs. Free cash flow turned positive at $34 million, marking our third straight quarter of FCF positivity—a key inflection point for SaaS peers as they navigate post-pandemic normalization.

Our trailing 12-month net cash burn has compressed to $12 million per month, down 35% year-over-year from aggressive cost optimization. This includes headcount discipline: We grew headcount only 4% YoY to 1,250 employees, with a focus on engineering—65% of hires—to accelerate features like our GenAI Workflow Builder, which is driving 30% faster onboarding and contributing to a 112% QBR in new logos. R&D efficiency at 28% of revenue yielded innovations like zero-ETL data pipelines that reduce customer TCO by 40%, positioning us competitively against Databricks in the analytics-adjacent space.

At current burn rates and conservative revenue projections, this translates to a robust 30+ months of runway—well beyond the 18-24 month benchmarks that give investors comfort. Even in a downside scenario with 10% lower ARR growth, we'd maintain 24 months, supported by our $750 million undrawn credit facility with JPMorgan and Silicon Valley Bank.

Regionally, our cash position benefits from diversified revenue streams: US at 62% of ARR with 42% YoY growth, led by financial services wins like a top-5 bank; EMEA at 25% with 55% growth via GDPR-compliant AI features, outpacing peers' European ramps; and APAC at 13% challenging at 28% growth due to yen volatility and China regulatory scrutiny, but offset by ANZ enterprise deals. We're strategically deploying $50 million into APAC localization next year, including Tokyo and Singapore data sovereignty builds.

Looking forward, our runway extends further through strategic levers: Rule of 40 mastery at 52—42% growth + 10% margin—on track for FCF margins of 25% by FY2026; M&A tuck-ins with $100 million dry powder for bolt-ons in vertical SaaS; share repurchase authorization of $75 million, signaling confidence amid our P/S multiple of 8.2x—attractive versus sector medians. Risks remain, like potential churn from economic slowdowns—though our <5% gross churn is best-in-class—forex impacts with 10% of ARR exposed, and competitive intensity from Microsoft's Copilot ecosystem. But with net dollar retention north of 115% and a $1.2 billion backlog, we're positioned to weather any storm.

On capital allocation strategy, which remains a cornerstone of our disciplined approach to driving long-term shareholder value in this dynamic SaaS landscape. We ended Q3 with a robust $1.4 billion in cash and equivalents, plus $800 million in undrawn credit facilities, giving us ample dry powder—about 18 months of runway at current burn rates even in a prolonged macro downturn. Our free cash flow generation continues to impress, supported by our industry-leading 128% net revenue retention and Rule of 40 score of 62.

Our philosophy is straightforward: prioritize high-ROI investments that accelerate ARR growth, expand our total addressable market, and fortify our competitive moat, while opportunistically returning capital to shareholders. In FY24 to date, we've deployed capital across key buckets, adjusted for our projected 22% ARR growth trajectory. First, organic R&D investments commanding a significant portion—this is table stakes in SaaS, where product velocity is king. We've doubled down on generative AI integrations across our core platform, akin to what Salesforce did with Einstein or ServiceNow with Vancouver releases. Specifically, we're investing $150 million this fiscal year in our Zenith AI Fabric equivalent, a composable, agentic AI layer that enables no-code workflows for enterprise customers. Early pilots with Fortune 500 clients like a major U.S. bank and a European telco are showing 35% uplift in user productivity and 18% reduction in churn risk. We're also allocating $80 million to zero-trust security enhancements and multi-region data sovereignty compliance, critical as we navigate GDPR 2.0 in EMEA and India's DPDP Act. Regionally, APAC now gets 22% of our R&D spend—up from 15% last year—to localize features for high-growth markets like Japan and Southeast Asia, where we're targeting 40% YoY expansion in RPO.

Second, M&A and strategic tuck-ins. In a market where public SaaS multiples have compressed to 6-8x ARR from the 15x peaks of 2021, we've been acquisitive but selective—focusing on IP and talent over revenue bolt-ons. Our recent crown jewel was the acquisition of a stealth-mode startup with proprietary vector databases that supercharge our analytics engine. This has already contributed meaningful ARR synergies, with cross-sell penetration hitting 62% in beta cohorts, mirroring Adobe's success with Marketo. We're also deploying into a venture arm for minority stakes in 10-15 early-stage SaaS plays—think AI ops tools like what Harness or Datadog are building—yielding strong returns on prior vintages. Looking ahead, with interest rates stabilizing around 4-5%, we expect 2-3 more tuck-ins in FY24, targeting EMEA cybersecurity and LatAm vertical SaaS to diversify our 65% North American revenue mix.

Third, share repurchases, representing an opportunistic portion of deployment. We've repurchased shares at an average discount to our intrinsic value based on 10x FCF multiples. This is opportunistic; we paused large blocks during dips but resumed aggressively post-earnings. No dividends yet—we're growth-focused like Workday or Snowflake—but we'll revisit if FCF exceeds thresholds annually.

Finally, the balance went to deleveraging, reducing net debt meaningfully. Minimal capex here, as our hyperscaler partnerships with AWS and Azure keep infrastructure opex variable.

Strategically, in this era of AI hyperscaling and economic uncertainty, we're threading the needle: 70% of capital into growth levers—R&D + M&A—to outpace peers' 15-18% ARR growth, while maintaining investment-grade balance sheet flexibility. Our CAC payback remains under 14 months, and we're monitoring trends like the 20% YoY rise in enterprise AI spend per Gartner. Risks include integration execution on deals and capex inflation from GPU shortages, but our $2.2 billion liquidity shields us. We're confident this allocation will deliver 25%+ EPS growth in FY24.

Moving to free cash flow performance, which continues to be a hallmark of CloudForge's asset-light SaaS model. For Q3 FY2024, we generated free cash flow of $152 million, representing a robust 42% year-over-year increase from $107 million in the prior-year quarter. This translates to a free cash flow margin of 25% of revenue, up 500 basis points from 20% a year ago and marking our eighth consecutive quarter of FCF margin expansion.

Free cash flow is calculated as cash provided by operating activities of $168 million—up 38% YoY—less capital expenditures of $16 million. Our operating cash flow benefited from strong collections efficiency, with days sales outstanding improving to 54 days from 62 days last year, driven by tighter credit policies with our enterprise customers and accelerated invoicing on multi-year deals. This is particularly noteworthy in a macro environment where elongated payment terms have pressured peers like Salesforce and Workday, who've reported DSOs in the high 60s.

Key drivers across our P&L and balance sheet levers, with a SaaS-specific lens: Revenue momentum and operating leverage, with total revenue up 32% YoY to $608 million adjusted for context, fueled by 28% dollar-based net retention and expansion within our top 500 customers, including major wins with Fortune 100 names in financial services and tech giants akin to our integrations with AWS and Snowflake. ARR ended at $2.4 billion normalized, up 30% YoY. This top-line strength converted efficiently to cash, as our non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 28%—ahead of guided range—thanks to sales and marketing efficiency. CAC payback shortened to 14 months from 16 months, reflecting higher win rates on our AI-powered CloudForge Optimizer module, which now contributes 15% of new ACV.

Working capital optimization: Cash from customers netted strongly, offset modestly by prepaids for data center capacity. We've leaned into our consumption-based pricing model—similar to Snowflake's approach—which aligns cash inflows with usage spikes during peak seasons for our analytics workloads. Deferred revenue grew 25% YoY, providing strong future cash visibility.

CapEx discipline: At just 2.6% of revenue, down from 3.2% YoY, as we capitalized on hyperscaler efficiencies. Over 90% of our infrastructure is now on public cloud, minimizing owned hardware needs. This keeps us firmly in the asset-light SaaS camp.

Regionally, North America drove 65% of the quarter's cash generation amid sticky enterprise renewals at 98% gross retention. EMEA contributed 20% growth in operating cash, bolstered by GDPR-compliant features that accelerated deals with European banks, though FX headwinds shaved margins slightly. APAC remains highest-growth at 55% YoY revenue but lower FCF conversion due to upfront sales investments in Japan and India—ramping localized data sovereignty for customers like major enterprises. We're targeting APAC FCF breakeven by Q1 FY2025 through cohort-based go-to-market scaling.

Strategically, our Rule of 40 score hit 57 this quarter—32% growth + 25% FCF margin—well above the SaaS benchmark and positioning us competitively against high-flyers like Datadog or CrowdStrike. We've deployed $100 million of this FCF into share repurchases under our $500 million authorization, retiring 1.2% of shares accretively. The balance supports tuck-in M&A, echoing bolt-on strategies to embed generative AI across workflows.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 FCF of $165-175 million, with full-year FY2024 FCF guidance raised to $620-640 million. This durability stems from our focus on product-led growth, where AI innovations are extending NRR into the mid-30s over time. Our FCF yield underscores a sustainable moat.

Finally, on operating margin performance, which continues to reflect the strong operating leverage we're generating as CloudForge scales. For Q3 FY2024, we delivered a non-GAAP operating margin of 18.2%, up 620 basis points year-over-year from 12.0% in Q3 FY2023, and up 110 basis points sequentially. On a GAAP basis, the margin was 14.5%, compared to 9.8% last year, with the difference primarily driven by stock-based compensation and amortization of acquisition intangibles.

This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of operating margin expansion, bringing us to 17.4% on a trailing twelve-month basis—well ahead of our long-term target of 25%+ by FY2026, in line with peers like ServiceNow and Snowflake as they mature beyond hyper-growth phases.

Revenue scale remains the biggest tailwind: Q3 revenue grew 35% year-over-year, fueled by 28% ARR growth, with dollar-based net retention of 118%—our highest in three quarters. This expansion, driven by upsells in our core platform for multi-cloud orchestration, allowed fixed costs to dilute meaningfully. Operating expenses grew just 22% year-over-year, giving us 1,300 basis points of leverage.

On the gross margin front, we expanded to 82.4% non-GAAP, up from 79.1% last year. Key initiatives include optimizing our AWS and Azure hyperscaler spend through reserved instances and spot pricing, which shaved 3 points off cost of revenue. We've also rolled out our proprietary AutoScale AI engine, which dynamically rightsizes compute resources for customer workloads, reducing hosting costs by an average of 22% for large-enterprise deployments—mirroring efficiencies at Databricks but tailored to our SaaS control plane.

Sales and marketing efficiency was another standout, with S&M at 42% of revenue, down from 48% last year. CAC payback period improved to 16 months from 20 months, thanks to accelerated product-led growth. Freemium trials for our new developer tools converted at 14%, versus 9% for traditional inbound, reducing reliance on field sales. We're now seeing LTV/CAC ratios above 5x for net-new logos, particularly in verticals like financial services where compliance modules are resonating—echoing HubSpot's playbook.

R&D spend held steady at 22% of revenue, but with higher output: we shipped 17 major features this quarter, including generative AI integrations with models from OpenAI and Anthropic for automated policy enforcement. Internal AI copilots have boosted engineer productivity by 30%, allowing us to maintain innovation velocity without headcount bloat.

G&A came in at 9% of revenue, benefiting from shared services consolidation post-acquisitions.

Regionally, North America drove 65% of revenue growth, with operating leverage strongest here at 22% margins due to mature go-to-market teams. EMEA margins improved to 15% on 45% YoY revenue growth, as we localized our platform for GDPR-heavy workloads and expanded partnerships with SAP and Oracle. APAC weighed on the blend at 8% margins amid upfront investments—data sovereignty builds in Japan and Australia—but revenue there surged 60% YoY, positioning us for 20%+ regional margins by FY2025.

Strategically, this positions us firmly within the Rule of 40, scoring 53 this quarter, and our free cash flow margin hit 22%. We're prioritizing operating leverage through AI automation across the stack—next up, sales copilot for deal acceleration and automated customer success playbooks to push NRR toward 125%. Headwinds include elevated stock-based comp at 12% of revenue due to retention grants, and macro caution in SMB segments, where win rates dipped slightly. But with a $4.2 billion RPO backlog up 40% YoY, visibility is high.

Overall, these margins underscore CloudForge's transition to a profitable compounder. We're raising our FY2024 non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 17-18%, from 16-17%, assuming continued macro stability.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first three quarters of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $1.1 billion to $1.2 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for a technology update.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers, including zero-ETL pipelines, agentic AI agents, and multi-cloud Kubernetes optimizations that handle petabyte-scale data with 99.99% uptime.

And now Lisa Chen will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Elena. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of ForgeEdge, our new edge AI inference feature. This new feature significantly improves real-time decisioning speeds by up to 40% for customer-facing workflows. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature, which aligns with our product strategy of embedding AI everywhere to boost productivity and retention.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, and how it compares to your initial expectations?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been a game-changer for our overall growth, contributing over 25% of new bookings in Q3 and accelerating our land-and-expand motion. We're seeing attach rates of 45% in existing enterprise customers, with upsell ACV averaging $250K per deal, particularly for modules like the Predictor and Security integrations. This is well ahead of our initial expectations, where we modeled 30% attach; the faster ramp is due to hyperscaler partnerships and early wins mirroring ServiceNow's AI adoption curves, positioning us for even stronger expansion in Q4.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Priya Patel:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, and what are your key target markets?

Jamie Thompson:
Great question, Priya. International expansion remains a top priority, with APAC as our fastest-growing region at 68% YoY. Our plans include $50 million in targeted investments for localization, including new data centers in Tokyo and Singapore to address sovereignty needs. Key target markets are e-commerce verticals with Shopify-like integrations for SMB scale, and enterprise banking in Mumbai and ANZ, where we're piloting POCs that leverage our GDPR-ready AI features adapted for local regs. We're aiming for APAC to hit 10% of ARR by FY25, building on 50/50 enterprise-SMB mix and partnerships like Tencent Cloud.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, and what are your strategies to improve customer retention?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, David. In this environment, we're managing churn proactively through AI-driven health scores and a revamped CS playbook, keeping gross churn under 5% overall—sub-2% in enterprise. NRR trended up to 118% this quarter, up 600 bps sequentially, driven by 28% expansion from AI upsells offsetting 6% churn and 4% contraction, mainly SMB normalization. Strategies for retention include ForgeAI predictive models that recovered 15% of at-risk accounts, expanded CS to 250 reps, and premium tiers tying value to outcomes; this has Day 90 activation at 92%, positioning Q4 NRR at 119-121%.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Jamie Thompson for closing remarks.

Jamie Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
